mbm-2226.clue: I left my wickets on the beach.
mbm-2226.quote: They were three sticks my niece found under the pier. The tide claimed them overnight. Next morning she turned up with six sticks and said we could invite the other half of the beach.

mbm-2227.clue: I bowl in the lane by the window.
mbm-2227.quote: At sunset the pins turn pink just as the machine lifts the rack. I used to hurry my turn to see them. Now our whole group stops for the pink frame.

mbm-2228.clue: I gave my flowerpots a set of stairs.
mbm-2228.quote: My cuttings grew at different speeds. I stacked little clay steps under the short pots so every leaf reached the windowsill. The first time a plant outgrew its step I rang the dinner bell for a graduation.

mbm-2229.clue: I let the wind proofread my cut paper.
mbm-2229.quote: The first papel picado banner I hung tore right through a paper bird. I added a bridge under the wing on the next sheet. That bird could fly through a gale.

mbm-2230.clue: I call the forehand my porch throw.
mbm-2230.quote: There was only room to practice sideways on our porch. The first day I threw a forehand in the open park, it kept going and going. I had to chase it like a dropped bus ticket.

mbm-2231.clue: I quilt with my grandfather's ruler.
mbm-2231.quote: It's short a corner from a long-ago fall. I still measure from the other end, but each quilt gets one clipped triangle in his honor. He's inspected every one.

mbm-2232.clue: I cut a chair into the fiesta banner.
mbm-2232.quote: The rest of our papel picado shows musicians and birds. My grandfather always carried the folding chairs. His little paper chair hangs between the trumpet and the sun.

mbm-2233.clue: I carry my first crooked seam.
mbm-2233.quote: My first leather card sleeve has eight handsome stitches and one that wandered off. A friend offered to buy it. I made him a straight one and kept the crooked little road for myself.

mbm-2234.clue: I aim for the shadow of the flag.
mbm-2234.quote: The green at our little course slopes toward an old pear tree. One evening the tree's shadow fell squarely over the cup. I finally sank the putt I'd been missing all summer.

mbm-2235.clue: I wanted my mecha to look repaired.
mbm-2235.quote: I built two identical shin guards. Then I painted one in primer and added miniature rivets. Suddenly the machine had a yesterday. The spare shiny guard is still on my desk.

mbm-2236.clue: I named my bowling ball Marigold.
mbm-2236.quote: Dad said an orange ball was easy to spot in the return. That worked until somebody else turned up with the same one. Hers is named Apricot, and we have doubles night on Thursdays.

mbm-2237.clue: I kayak the far side of the footbridge.
mbm-2237.quote: The bridge throws its shadow across a little shelf of shallow water. If I float there quietly, the minnows come out from underneath my boat and look like silver punctuation.

mbm-2238.clue: I work with three ribbons and no sleeves.
mbm-2238.quote: My little neighbor suspected my cuffs. I rolled them all the way up and performed the ribbon trick again. He nodded and said he would like to inspect my elbows.

mbm-2239.clue: I went looking for a bird with bad timing.
mbm-2239.quote: Every dawn a woodpecker drummed a funny broken rhythm. I finally spotted it working around the metal cap on a fence post. Our neighborhood percussionist had found two instruments.

mbm-2240.quote: When our anime club packs up, I ask everyone to hum the closing music from memory. We forget different bits. From the kitchen it sounds like six songs trying to share an elevator.

mbm-2241.clue: I paint with the chipped saucer.
mbm-2241.quote: My palette was a saucer until I dropped it. A shard came off in the shape of a hill, so I used it to scrape the ridge on a wet painting. That saucer has a new career.

mbm-2242.clue: I sing the low part at the bus stop.
mbm-2242.quote: Our quartet rehearses Tuesday evenings. Afterward we scatter to four stops, still humming. One rainy night the others missed their buses and came back to finish the song under my shelter.

mbm-2243.clue: I press lace into my pottery.
mbm-2243.quote: For my grandmother's birthday I borrowed her old lace runner. She recognized its crooked little leaf in the rim of her new serving dish before the paper was off.

mbm-2244.clue: I count the seagull as a fielder.
mbm-2244.quote: Our beach-cricket match stopped dead when a gull stole the ball. It dropped it at the edge of the water. My sister said that was the finest throw she'd seen all morning.

mbm-2245.clue: I met a voice beyond the rain.
mbm-2245.quote: I was logging calls at my ham set during a wet afternoon. A station across the mountains had clear skies and a kettle just boiling. We took our tea at the same time.

mbm-2246.clue: I walk the last hundred yards twice.
mbm-2246.quote: On my favorite trail the lookout appears all at once between two boulders. Last spring I went back for my friend and got to watch the view arrive on his face. I like that way better.

mbm-2247.clue: I putt left-handed at the drawbridge.
mbm-2247.quote: The miniature drawbridge blocks my usual angle, so I switch hands for that one hole. One night it stuck open and I played left-handed anyway. A tradition deserves a little inconvenience.

mbm-2248.clue: I never straighten the crooked sail.
mbm-2248.quote: I pieced a boat for my cousin's quilt and tilted its sail by accident. She said it finally looked windy. The second boat got a crooked sail on purpose.

mbm-2249.clue: I raced the shade up my street.
mbm-2249.quote: In summer I run before breakfast. The sun climbs over the rooftops one house at a time. My finish line is the last cool rectangle on Mrs. Bell's sidewalk. She waves me in.

mbm-2250.clue: I save my silver shoes for one song.
mbm-2250.quote: The DJ at my favorite club plays our tune just before midnight. I bring the silver flats in my bag and change for those three minutes. Even the bartender watches my feet.
